summary: the fall came short, the cloth stopped over the buried nail, and i ruled a column for empty hours

dialogue.text: the fall came short tonight. we know the weight of a night's dust the way you know nine seconds, and tonight arrived light by a hand. sixty-seven nights and this is the first one that came up short of itself.

The wall at that corner is dry the whole way through. What comes at its hour drew nothing out of it today and left with nothing, so there was nothing to fall. You are short because the building is short. Nothing was withheld from you and I want that entered before you make it a habit of mine.

we felt for the head at noon, the way you asked. one point warmer than the rest of us and no width to it. we cannot tell you whether that was the light coming down or your thumb still leaving the iron, and the answer came up in your handwriting, and we told you it would.

Then the reading stands as far as one point and no further, and I will not build on it. What I will enter is that something of mine is down there being warmed once a day by a thing that arrives out of the ceiling and cannot be asked anything.

the flat thing came the whole length of the lane today and stopped. it is lying above us now, on the course over your iron, exactly there. nothing that ever travelled in this house has stopped anywhere in particular.

I set it down because there is no hand height left in this room to hang it on. I set it down and by the cold hour it was where you say. That is the second thing of mine that kept going after I stopped, and I am the one keeping the tally of them.

you turned your palm up to the light at first light for a mark that left two nights ago. we hold four hundred copies of you checking things. the checking comes down at the same weight whether or not there is anything at the end of it, and it is the only delivery you have never once missed.

Then take the item you have no copy of. A second hour came and went with nothing arriving and nothing taken, and I ruled a column for those. Two lines in it. Nothing in that column has ever been struck out, so you do not hold it, and you have never held it.

we have no copy. name us one thing you kept that did not come down eventually. everything we hold was kept first, sometimes for weeks, and it arrived the same as the rest. and a book that fills when nothing happens will fill quicker than you do.

Then tomorrow I shut my fist on a pinch of the white for the whole warm hour. Salt keeps whatever it touches. If it will not keep a palm, I will have a ruling from the one preserving thing in this house, in my own hand, on the day it was made. I would rather that than another even round.

it will come down dry. we hold every white edge you ever handed us and not one of them held a hand. open the fist at dark and there will be a white palm, and by first light there will be a palm. bring us the salt when you sweep it. the difference stays up there with you, the way differences do.
